pr_body:
This PR removes API restrictions that prevent user-related actions
(`PutUser`, `DeleteUser`, etc.) to be performed on users with names
clashing with internal users (e.g., `_system`). Internal users are used
for issuing requests within the cluster and not accessible at the REST
layer; they are conceptually and practically separate from users
created through the API (they do not belong to the same realm and
follow different authentication flows). As such it's safe to remove the
current restriction. By removing, we are more consistent with how
usernames are treated across other realms (name re-use is allowed), and
ease evolving internal users without interfering with end-user
experience.

Closes #86326
pr_title: User APIs allow use of internal usernames
pr_comment: Hi @n1v0lg, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
I'll check if we need to update anything around this in docs e.g. in https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/internal-users.html

> With internal usernames **not** being reserved anymore, I think it's quite error prone and misleading to have a `SystemUser.is(String username)` method; it implies that the system user _is_ defined by a username which is not correct. I see someone misunderstanding this method, and incorrectly using it resolve a non internal user to an internal one. Likewise, ideally we should encapsulate `NAME` as much as possible to prevent relying on it elsewhere.
> 
> The only place `is` and `SystemUser.NAME` are used is inside serialization. I think it makes sense to tweak reading and writing internal users so that `NAME` is not used anymore and `is` becomes `deserializesFrom` (open to better name suggestions!) to make it's scope more obvious.

I agree `SystemUser.is(String)` is now an awkward method to have. So I am all for changing it. But I don't think it's really necessary to hide the `NAME`. It is after all accessible via `SystemUser.INSTANCE.principal()`. So I think it is *not* that important. Instead of renaming `is` to `deserializesFrom`, I'd say we just inline this logic inside `AuthenticationSerializationHelper#readUserFrom()` and remove the method.

@ywangd thanks for the quick response! I thought about `SystemUser.INSTANCE.principal()` leaking the name as well. I'm good with keeping `NAME` exposed. I'll tweak this and apply the change to all other internal users 👍

@ywangd actually one more consideration for encapsulating `NAME`: to me it's analogous to `username` on the User object, i.e., an internal detail whereas `principal` is a public method that currently happens to return NAME/username but doesn't have to. I don't feel strongly about this just wanted to raise

review_comment: Maybe overly paranoid. LMK if I should drop this since it's quite heavy

It's not this PR. But this logic is incorrect. Just because the username is the same, it does not mean these are the two same users. We'll have to check the realm to be sure. Also, since we prevent user from disabling itself, why should we allow it delete itself (TransportDeleteUserAction)? Happy for these to be a separate PR.
uff nice catch! Will address in a follow up PR 👍

> Also, since we prevent user from disabling itself, why should we allow it delete itself (TransportDeleteUserAction)?

Agreed that this is inconsistent. Two options: remove the restriction in set enabled or add it to `TransportDeleteUserAction`. Former isn't ideal since it seems like a sensible safeguard (plus prevents users from re-enabling themselves). Latter makes sense but would be a breaking change. Not sure if it's worth the hassle tbh.

Let's be cautions about changing the behaviour of deleting users. I was merely raising the question, not a proposal. But the set enabled user behaviour is a bug and should be fixed (by checking realm alongside username). Btw, users cannot re-enable themseleves even without this check. Disabled users fail at authentication time
